newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG factions pledge to work for lasting peace.
newsitem.headline: PNG factions pledge to work for lasting peace.

text.p: Representatives of warring factions on Papua New Guinea's Bougainville Island pledged on Saturday to work towards a lasting solution to the secessionist crisis at peace talks in New Zealand. Representatives of the three main groups in the hostilities, the PNG-backed Bougainville Transitional Government (BTG), the Bougainville Interim Government (BIG) and its associate the Bougainville Revolutionary Army (BRN), were flown into New Zealand early this morning.
"These talks are a very important step towards trying to solve the Bougainville crisis," said Gerard Sinato, Premier of the BTG.
"The very important thing we have in mind is to end the war and get peace in our beautiful land."

New Zealand Foreign Minister Don McKinnon, who welcomed the meeting's 50 participants onto Burnham Military Camp near the South Island city of Christchurch, said he hoped for progress in the preliminary discussions.
The initial talks only involve Bougainville parties.
"I have talked to members of the Papua New Guinean government. They are very supportive of what is happening here," McKinnon told reporters after the official welcome.

BIG/BRA representative Joseph Kabui said there was a will on both sides of the crisis to broker a solution. "There is a groundswell on both sides of Bougainville, on the BTG side and on the BIG/BRA side, for reconciliation and peace," he said.
However, several delegates from resistance groups on Bougainville opposed to the BRA were prevented from attending the talks when the helicopter sent to pick them up was fired upon.
Kabui said one or two BRA members acting alone were responsible for the incident and it was a case of indiscriminant fire rather than a planned attack.

"It will not deter the peace process," he said, adding that the people involved would be disciplined. McKinnon said the formal talks, scheduled to begin on Monday, would run for at least a week and it was hoped more delegates would arrive during the week.
"We hope you find this neutral environment...conducive to discussing your issues," he told the delegates.
Thousands have died in fighting on the resource-rich island which lies to the southeast of the main Papua New Guinea archipelago and neighbours the Solomon Islands.
Previous attempts at internationally-brokered peace talks since the early 1990s have failed to produce concrete results.
"History tells us there is no easy way through this process, but that is no reason for you not to try and lay a solid foundation here at Burnham for future discussions," McKinnon added.
